newsitem.title: BOSNIA: NATO finds booby-traps in former Moslem village.
newsitem.headline: NATO finds booby-traps in former Moslem village.

text.p: NATO said on Sunday that peacekeepers found booby-trap mines in a former Moslem village in Bosnian Serb territory, underscoring rising tensions along a wartime front line.
NATO officers said the incident appeared to be the latest attempt by Serbs to discourage Moslems from moving back to their homes in northeast Bosnia.
Soldiers in the NATO-led peace force (IFOR) discovered eight anti-tank mines booby-trapped to a power station in the ruined Moslem village of Koraj, north of Sapna, a NATO spokesman said.
If detonated, the mines could have caused serious damage to the station, Major Brett Boudreau told reporters.
"Although we have no hard evidence to blame Serbs for it, there are only a couple of plausible explanations why this is happening," Boudreau said.
Koraj is currently abandoned but NATO says Moslems may try to return to the village, which lies in the strategic Sapna region.
The discovery of booby-traps reflected an atmosphere of mistrust and fear pervading in northeastern villages formerly inhabited by Moslems.
Moslem authorities say Serbs are blowing up houses they are trying to rebuild in a bid to obstruct the return of refugees.
The Serbs accuse the Moslems of bringing in arms which are banned inside the demilitarised "zone of separation" along the former front line.
NATO reported earlier that three houses were damaged by explosions on Thursday in the nearby village of Kovacevici, which had a predominantly Moslem population.

The NATO peace force has been collecting data on explosion reports from the past few weeks in Moslem villages which are either currently being resettled or may be possible targets for resettlement, Boudreau said.
